findings.issue: Still open from the last review: the 40-word hero lead still sits on the photo. At 390 px it runs five centred lines under the two-line H1 and fills the whole 275 px band. At 1440 px it takes three lines under the 88 px title in a 293 px band. Either way the photo reads only as dark texture behind text.
findings.reference: The competitor's matching page (its about page) puts only its bold title on the photo, with no lead. Its running text starts on white under the photo band.
findings.fix: BlogHubView.astro already has a leadBelow path, but heroLeadShown() with the site-wide heroText.leadWords lets this lead onto the photo. Make the on-photo lead limit apply per page type (the reference page has 0 lead words), so that .blog-hub-hero__lead renders under the banner on white and only the H1 stays on the photo.

findings.issue: Still open from the last review: the three plain sections after the hero (overview, overview-steps, table-1) still all sit on white, one under another, at both widths, so only padding separates them.
findings.reference: The site's rule, which follows the competitor's banded pages, is that neighbouring plain sections alternate white and tinted backgrounds.
findings.fix: The template's alternation on the blog hub should give overview-steps, which sits between the white overview and the white table-1, the var(--section-tint) background. Do not add a rule in reference.css for this one section.

findings.issue: Still open from the last review: at 390 px the H1 'The Strandmill Blog' (38 px) still breaks into a centred 'The Strandmill', with the one word 'Blog' alone on its second line.
findings.reference: The competitor's phone hero title keeps to its line and leaves no word alone on its last line.
findings.fix: The template's title fit should balance a two-line page title at phone widths (text-wrap: balance on .blog-hub-hero h1) or size this short title to one line. Set no fixed font-size in reference.css.

findings.issue: Still open from the last review: at 390 px the hero is still a 275 px band cut from a wide photo and covered by text, so the photo barely reads.
findings.reference: The competitor's phone hero shows its factory photo as a tall portrait frame, about 550 px high at 390 px wide, with only the title over it.
findings.fix: Let the hero take a portrait crop or a separate portrait photo on phones (art direction per breakpoint). Stretching the wide photo's frame would cut the photo away.

findings.issue: Still open from the last review: each of the ten outlined cards repeats the same grey label 'What this means for you' between its title and its text. The label adds nothing, makes the set read as boilerplate, and adds ten lines to a stack of about 3,100 px at 390 px.
findings.reference: The competitor's outlined cards carry only a bold title and its text, with no repeated label.
findings.fix: Site Factory should drop the repeated 'What this means for you' column label from the table-1 rows, so each card shows its title and then its text.
